label: End of a length-9 input: last original token (r/k/b/g/j/...) and the <DEL> step
explanation: A positional unit for the end of long inputs. It fires almost only at absolute steps 7-9, and nearly all activation mass (about 95%) is in L=9 sequences: on the 9th original token (t=8, about 46% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (t=9, about 47%). A small remainder is in L=8 at t=7/8. It never fires in the copy phase after <DEL>, and never before t=7. The plain positional predicate (L==9 & t in {8,9}) gets recall 0.87 and mass recall 0.93, but precision is only 0.34, so firing is token-gated. At t=8 it prefers certain input letters (r strongest, then k, b, g, j, p, n; y rarely). At <DEL> it prefers sequences whose first token, which is about to be output, is a digit (2, 1, 3) or h/y/x/i/l/q/u/g. The top activations are on r at t=8 of L=9. Token gating is only roughly captured by these lists.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: r, k, b, j, p, g; least: v, i, d, c) and the first original token (most: 2, 1, h, y, 3, x; least: f, z, e, a); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=8, L=9 & t=9.
